newsitem.title: USA: Second storm forecast for southern, Midwest U.S.
newsitem.headline: Second storm forecast for southern, Midwest U.S.

text.p: Residents from Texas to New England will have a few days to recover from the latest snow storm before a second system of equal strength develops in western Texas and moves northeast, meteorologists said.

More than six inches of snow fell the past few days along a line from south central Texas to Ohio. Weather maps suggest the next system will develop by early Friday in western Texas and from Saturday through Monday will move across central Arkansas, southern Illinois and Indiana and into New England.
"It looks pretty wet and very similar to the one we just had," said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist."

Gesser said that rain should occur ahead of the advancing storm system changing to snow along the system's northern boundaries after the front passes. The moisture could create problems for cattle in feedlots, but otherwise low temperatures and moisture associated with the system were not expected to present severe problems for the livestock industry, he said.
Prior to Friday, cold weather should blanket much of the Midwest with low temperatures averaging six to 12 degrees below normal, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Burgio said highs this week in the Midwest should range from mid 20s to low 30s Fahrenheit, and lows from single digits to mid-teens.
